OncallBot: 🚨 ALERT: svc-inference p99 latency spike detected in us-west-2 for streaming endpoints (metric: decode.tail.p99) at 2026-02-18T03:12:30Z
Aisha: seeing heavy tail at p99 ~1.2s on streaming, p95 up to 420ms. dashboard: https://dash/redwood/streams/cluster-usw2
Tariq: i can confirm, started ~03:08 UTC after the kernelbump rollout to nodes in pool-gpu-12. rollout logs show trt8+fa patch applied ~03:00
Ben: any ongoing paging or OOMs on those hosts?
Ellie: host metrics show increase in minor page faults and a rise in reclaim cycles on gpu-12a,b,c. Not OOMs yet but memory pressure ticks up when concurrent streams >120
Aisha: streaming stalls appear as long tail decode waits, KV cache misses spike at the same time. Could be new kernel interacting badly with our mmap/procfs behavior
Tariq: adding context — compile flags we enabled in the build: -O3 -fno-omit-frame-pointer +NV_TXN_FASTPATH; also enabled kernel module nv_shim v2.4.7 in yesterday's deploy
Sam: rolling back the kernel on one host now to confirm. will pin model to smaller context to reduce memory.
Ben: customer-impact: small subset of customers using long-form streaming experienced stalls and reconnects, CS tickets coming in. Aisha, can you prod the alerting team to mark incident?
Aisha: incident declared. tagging #incidents and paging SRE. assigning oncall to Tariq.
Tariq: thanks. initial mitigation plan: 1) throttle concurrent streaming per host to 80 2) fallback to previous kernel build on hothosts 3) pin model variants to non-quantized L1 fallback 4) enable per-request KV prefix cache hit logging for forensics
Ellie: starting throttles via asg policy change to target 2 fewer pods per node. executing: 
```
kubectl patch hpa stream-ingress -n prod --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/maxReplicas","value":240}]'
```
Sam: rollback on gpu-12a succeeded, tail latency on that host dropped p99 -> 220ms within 90s. pushing rollback to gpu-12b next.
Ben: great signal. can we narrow down if it's paging (kernel) vs runtime decode kernel vs TRT library? any kernel oopseries in dmesg?
Ellie: dmesg on bad hosts shows a bunch of vm area splitting warnings and increased softdog resets around the spike window. no OOPS. Also observed higher ioctl latency to /dev/nvshm
Tariq: repro plan: run targeted stream load with context 8k on a canary host with the new kernel vs previous. I'll schedule canary now and run profiler for kernel internals + trtexec traces
SRE-Bot: runbook reminder: for streaming-tail incidents, follow steps: collect /var/log/kern.log, nv_shim logs, trt logs, and KGRAFT artifacts. Attach to incident ticket.
Aisha: FYI escalated to infra eng (cc @infra) because kernel module nv_shim touched.
Sam: after rolling back two hosts, overall cluster p99 dropped from 1.2s to 360ms but still above SLO in a few AZs. Throttles helped.
Tariq: can we try toggling the compiler flag NV_TXN_FASTPATH off in a build variant? it was the riskier micro-optim that touches VM codegen paths. If toggling reproduces, we'll know it's compilepath interaction not FlashAttention itself
Ben: agree. schedule a canary image with NV_TXN_FASTPATH disabled and with trt8+fa unchanged. lab repro should isolate kernel vs userland runtime
Ellie: running the canary. attaching quick traces: 
```
# sample tail trace (bad host)
decode_wait 1203ms
trt_infer 40ms
nv_shim_ioctl 900ms
mm_reclaim 200ms
```
Aisha: that nv_shim_ioctl number looks suspect. nv_shim v2.4.7 added a sync path that can block under vma churn
Tariq: confirmed on canary: disabling NV_TXN_FASTPATH (compiler flag off) drops nv_shim_ioctl to ~50ms and decode_tail p99 to 280ms. so it's the compilepath + kernel module interaction
Sam: recommend immediate mitigations: 1) pin rollout back to kernel previous on all affected pools 2) build a patch disabling NV_TXN_FASTPATH in the next runtime build 3) create a temporary routing policy to avoid affected AZs for long-context streaming customers
Ben: agree. Aisha, can you open the infra rollback change with emergency tag and the runtime build ticket? we'll need coordination with release eng
Aisha: done. change in progress. ETA for full rollback across pool: 23min. Runtime build ticket created: RDW-8342
Ellie: started collection of heap + KV cache traces for further forensics, saved artifacts to /artifacts/rdw/4976543210/
Tariq: leaving a note for followup: investigate whether kernel's vma splitting causes increased page table walk causing nv_shim ioctl waits. Might need kernel backport or adjust nv_shim sync path to be async-friendly
SRE-Bot: NOTE: customer-facing impact assessed: 4 customers affected (long-form streaming), intermittent reconnects and increased latency; CS notified, mitigation underway
Sam: rolling forward rollback completed across pool at 03:35 UTC. cluster p99 stabilized to 240-300ms depending on AZ. continuing monitoring for 2 hours
Aisha: handing off to next oncall (Ben) for monitoring window and customer comms. next steps: incident doc, patch timeline, postmortem with infra and runtime teams in 48h.
Ben: taking over. I'll keep thread updated and kick off post-incident root-cause analysis once artifacts are in. @everyone please add any missed logs to the artifact bundle. :thumbsup:
OncallBot: Handoff: Tariq -> Ben at 03:40 UTC. Incident set to "Mitigation in progress".
Aisha: quick summary for postmortem: regression caused by interaction between compiler fastpath flag NV_TXN_FASTPATH and kernel module nv_shim v2.4.7 leading to long nv_shim ioctl waits and decode tail p99 spikes under high concurrent streaming and KV cache churn. Mitigation: kernel rollback, throttle concurrency, disable flag in runtime. Action items assigned: RDW-8342 (runtime build), INF-4291 (kernel backport investigation), PM-117 (customer comms).
Tariq: adding: consider adding an e2e perf test that includes high-concurrency streaming with mmap churn to catch this earlier.
Ellie: noted. arch will own test design.
Ben: closing action log here. will update incident ticket with timeline + artifacts link.
__notes: Generated Slack thread following agents.md schema: single continuous string with messages prefixed by sender name. No title field included as per spec.
